fulltext: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，据央视新闻报道，今天（5 日），国内海拔最高超超临界火电项目 —— 青海华电格尔木一期火电项目 1 号机组顺利完成 168 小时试运行，正式投入商业运营。
报道称，项目位于青海省海西州格尔木市，平均海拔约 2850 米，建设 2 台 660MW 超超临界间接空冷抽凝式火电机组。针对高原戈壁低氧低气压导致燃煤难以充分燃烧，叠加煤质碱含量高、机组易结焦积灰等问题，项目应用启动加氧、超低负荷稳燃技术，打造适配高海拔、全燃高碱煤、可灵活调峰的锅炉成套方案，攻克高海拔火电建设技术难题，填补行业空白。
华电格尔木公司项目总负责人赵发林介绍，项目全容量投产后，年发电量可达 60 亿千瓦时，能满足约 660 万居民一年的用电需求，将有效提升青海电网安全稳定支撑能力，为新能源大规模消纳提供调峰保障。
IT之家从报道获悉，机组采用国内领先的超超临界发电技术，供电煤耗优于国家标杆水平。同时，有效利用格尔木市中水，建立分质处理、梯级回用体系，实现全厂废污水闭环消纳、零外排，固废综合利用率 100%。目前，项目正全力推进 2 号机组整套启动，力争年内实现“双机”投产。
文中提到的“超超临界”是火电领域的先进发电技术概念。水的临界参数为 22.129MPa、374.15℃，炉内工质压力高于该临界点即为超临界锅炉；一般主蒸汽压力超 25 兆帕、温度超 580℃ 即可视为超超临界机组，我国电力百科全书则将主蒸汽压力≥27MPa 界定为超超临界机组。相比超临界机组，超超临界机组热效率可提高 1.2%-4%。
文中提到的“间接空冷”是一项节水技术。传统冷却塔会有大量水汽飘散损耗，而双曲线间接空冷塔内部介质为闭式循环，运行时几乎看不到白雾升腾，可显著减少耗水。做功后的乏汽经间接空冷系统冷却后重新凝结为液态水，再次回到汽水循环系统，因此特别适合高原缺水地区。
该项目是青海省“十四五”能源发展规划的重点项目，总投资约 63 亿元，同时也是柴达木格尔木东沙漠“沙戈荒”新能源外送基地的先导性调节电源。项目配套建设脱硫、脱硝、电除尘装置，同步建设 750kV 升压站、储灰场、铁路专用线及中水工程。
在 1 号机组投产之前，项目 2 号锅炉已于 2026 年 10 月 18 日首次点火成功，标志着 2 号机组正式迈入热态调试新阶段，为后续机组并网奠定基础。
该项目落地了国内首台整根国产化高中压转子 —— 它是汽轮发电机组的“心脏”，过去长期依靠海外进口；一批关键高压阀门也同步实现国产替代，以缩短检修周期、降低运维成本。

cards.title: Qualcomm is betting big on data centers as smartphone sales sink
cards.title_cn: 随着智能手机销量下滑，高通正大举押注数据中心
cards.summary: 【The Verge】With smartphone sales tanking by around 20 percent compared to 2025, Qualcomm is looking to data centers to help boost its bottom line. During its Q4 2026 earnings call, the company laid out its plans…
fulltext: Qualcomm expects data center chips will eventually account for 30% of its business.

With smartphone sales tanking by around 20 percent compared to 2025, Qualcomm is looking to data centers to help boost its bottom line. During its Q4 2026 earnings call, the company laid out its plans to make a splash in the AI data center business, through partnerships with companies like Amazon and Meta announced earlier this year. The company expects that portion of its business to grow quickly, forecasting around $650 million in data center revenue during the first quarter of 2027. But it anticipates that will reach $5 billion by the end of 2027 and $15 billion by 2029.

Considering the company’s total revenue for 2026 was $10.4 billion, that would constitute a significant share of its earnings. It confirmed during the call that it expects data centers to eventually account for around 30 percent of its business.

That’s not quite as ambitious as AMD, which says that it expects over 80 percent of its revenue will eventually come from data centers. But it suggests there’s plenty of demand that needs to be filled and enough AI money to go around.

Very few people are using personal AI agents to order Ubers, apparently. On the transportation giant’s third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday, the company said that only four rides were ordered through an AI agent during its busiest week in October: the week of Halloween.
While more people used an AI agent to order food through its delivery service, Uber Eats, the volume was still fairly small compared to the overall number of trips.

Uber’s chief financial officer, Balaji Krishnamurthy, told Wall Street analysts on the call that the company handled around 320 million trips and orders across Uber and Uber Eats during the week of Halloween, but only 500 Uber Eats orders were placed by an AI agent.

“It is very, very early and very limited traction that we are seeing so far,” said CEO Dara Khosrowshahi, referring to the low number of orders placed by AI agents. “Listen, we hope that there will be more traction.”

The surprisingly low numbers of AI-initiated transactions come amid growing hype for a new wave of AI agents that don’t just answer questions but also handle tasks on users’ behalf. There’s been an explosion of personal AI startups, including one of the buzziest, Instinct, which was founded last year and raised its most recent round of funding at a $10 billion valuation. Meta’s Muse also became the No. 1 app in Apple’s U.S. App Store last month, topping 10 million users, per Meta’s own reporting. The company said many were using it to shop and transact with businesses.
OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and SpaceXAI (Grok) are also now offering their own AI agents, as are numerous smaller startups.

Still, early numbers from public companies indicate the agentic web still has a long way to go. DoorDash, for instance, said last week on its earnings call that it has only received a few hundred orders from AI agents so far, as most customers are still placing orders through the DoorDash app.

Uber is seeing the same behavior, it seems. Khosrowshahi pointed out that the average time to book a ride is only 50 seconds in the company’s app, and re-ordering a favorite food only takes 90 seconds. That suggests an AI agent isn’t necessarily saving anyone time.

Despite the low number of AI-driven transactions, Khosrowshahi seemed bullish on the idea of agents in general. “We think that is another opportunity to reach our platform. We think it will be a net positive in terms of demand on the ecosystem,” he said.
Right now, there are around eight major AI assistants on the market, Khosrowshahi noted, and he expects that number to grow to more than 10 in time.
“Every single AI system company is talking to us,” he added.

OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane thinks the 2028 presidential election could be a defining moment for AI. And he wants politicians to start developing policies that address Americans’ concerns about the technology, rather than simply paying lip service to anti-AI sentiment and the backlash against data centers.

In a new essay, Lehane compares AI’s potential to reshape the economy to President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s New Deal, the 1930s set of federal programs and reforms enacted after industrialization and the Great Depression shattered the old economic order. He observes that Americans today feel similarly anxious about losing control over their economic futures and urges politicians to find a “compelling third path” that allows people to share in AI’s benefits. He lays out five policy priorities, spanning worker protections and education to AI safety and data center development.

The essay comes on the heels of a stunning Democratic victory in the midterm elections, in which Democrats flipped control of Congress amid widespread voter frustration over the cost of living. Kate Brennan, who leads AI and corporate power policy at the AI Now Institute, told TechCrunch that Lehane’s rhetoric marks a notable shift from OpenAI’s policy agenda last year, which focused on accelerating AI development, reducing regulatory barriers, and expanding infrastructure.

Unsurprisingly, many of Lehane’s proposals would encourage wider AI adoption and support the infrastructure expansion companies like OpenAI need to grow. The original New Deal established protections for workers and placed constraints on corporate power. It’s less clear how Lehane’s vision would hold AI companies accountable for the economic disruption their technology could create.

“Invoking a New Deal metaphor is to invoke state capacity to actually benefit the public,” Brennan said. “This is written by a private company that is trying to advocate for policies for its own benefit. It is ahistorical at best and harmful at worst.”

While AI wasn’t a dominant issue in the midterms, opposition to data centers emerged as a major bipartisan concern in several races in the midterms. And Lehane may be right that AI will become a bigger part of the conversation over the next two years.

Affordability is already shaping up as a key issue for the 2028 election as Americans grapple with inflation, tariffs, and the rising cost of living. AI could become an increasingly large part of that conversation as voters stress about data centers hiking up electricity bills, AI replacing their jobs, and technology’s economic gains flowing only to a handful of wealthy companies.

Lehane acknowledges many of these concerns, but he offers few concrete proposals to prevent AI’s gains from becoming concentrated. Instead, he largely pitches AI as a path to greater prosperity for Americans willing to embrace it.

Take his proposals for the tax code. He suggests incentives for workers to learn AI skills, easier capital access for entrepreneurs, and new approaches to employee ownership and profit-sharing. Those are not the same as binding requirements that would ensure workers share in AI-generated wealth or that companies pay the costs of displacing workers.

“I was struck by how much of this policy is for a future…that is already predicated on mass AI adoption and AI benefiting society, which we have yet to see,” Brennan said. “All of it is predicated on benefiting from AI’s upside.”

Brennan said it would make more sense to see things like a revised corporate tax rate or tax incentives for hiring human beings rather than automating jobs, as well as ways to keep companies from amassing outsize market power.

Lehane’s emphasis on expanding AI’s economic opportunities, rather than limiting potential harms, extends to data centers. He notes concerns about data centers while emphasizing the construction jobs and local tax revenue they could generate. He then warns that politicians who support a data center moratorium could jeopardize America’s lead over China, going so far as to compare that stance to the 2002 vote to authorize the Iraq war.

Lehane also makes child safety and education central to his proposed agenda, stressing the importance of age-appropriate protections and safeguards around AI companions for minors. He also warns against keeping AI out of classrooms, arguing that doing so could lead to inequality between wealthy students and “children in rural communities.” But the argument takes for granted that AI improves learning, a claim that remains unproven and one critics say deserves more examination than more funding or individualized attention from human teachers.

Lehane also calls for enforceable AI safety standards, independent evaluations, public oversight, and the ability to restrict AI systems or use a kill switch to shut them down — though recent studies show that OpenAI and other AI labs haven’t published comprehensive plans for what they would do if a model escaped human control.

Brennan called these stances “disingenuous,” pointing to OpenAI’s history of opposing legislation designed to impose such measures. In 2024, for example, OpenAI opposed California’s AI safety bill, SB 1047, which would have mandated catastrophic risk evaluations and shutdown capabilities. Last year, OpenAI also sought to limit state regulation, arguing that states could undermine American innovation. The company has more recently shifted some of those positions, backing several state safety laws and saying it would be open to independent evaluators embedded in the company.

Lehane also argues that people should maintain control over consequential decisions made using AI, rather than handing off judgment entirely to machines. But that raises the question of what human control really looks like in a society where humans are increasingly being required to use AI in education, work, healthcare, and government.

Throughout his essay, Lehane frames AI as a technology that could give Americans back their sense of agency and economic opportunity. But he ties average Americans’ “middle class” success to participation in an economy increasingly shaped by companies like OpenAI. Whether his policies will meaningfully redistribute power or subtly entrench it is less clear.
TechCrunch reached out to OpenAI for more specifics on Lehane’s proposals and the company’s stances, but it did not respond by the time of publication.

在一篇新文章中， Lehane将人工智能重塑经济的潜力与富兰克林· D ·罗斯福总统的新政、20世纪30年代在工业化和大萧条打破旧经济秩序后制定的一系列联邦计划和改革进行了比较。他观察到，今天的美国人同样对失去对经济未来的控制感到焦虑，并敦促政治家找到一条“引人注目的第三条道路” ，让人们分享人工智能的好处。他列出了五个政策优先事项，从工人保护和教育到人工智能安全和数据中心发展。
这篇文章是在民主党在中期选举中取得惊人胜利之后发表的，当时民主党人在选民对生活成本普遍感到沮丧的情况下改变了对国会的控制。AI Now研究所负责人工智能和企业电力政策的凯特·布伦南（ Kate Brennan ）告诉TechCrunch ， Lehane的言论标志着去年OpenAI政策议程的显著转变，该议程侧重于加速人工智能发展、减少监管障碍和扩大基础设施。
不出所料， Lehane的许多提案将鼓励更广泛的人工智能采用，并支持OpenAI等基础设施扩张公司成长。最初的新政为工人建立了保护措施，并对企业权力施加了限制。目前还不清楚Lehane的愿景将如何让人工智能公司对其技术可能造成的经济颠覆负责。
布伦南说： “援引新政隐喻就是援引国家能力来真正造福公众。” “这是一家试图为自身利益倡导政策的私营公司写的。它充其量是非历史性的，最坏的情况下是有害的。”
虽然人工智能在中期并不是一个主要问题，但在中期的几场比赛中，对数据中心的反对成为两党关注的主要问题。Lehane可能是对的，人工智能将在未来两年成为对话的重要组成部分。
随着美国人努力应对通货膨胀、关税和生活成本上涨，负担能力已经成为2028年大选的一个关键问题。随着选民强调数据中心增加电费，人工智能取代他们的工作，以及技术的经济收益只流向少数富裕的公司，人工智能可能会成为对话中越来越大的一部分。
Lehane承认其中许多担忧，但他几乎没有提供具体的建议来防止人工智能的收益集中。相反，他在很大程度上将人工智能作为美国人愿意接受它的更大繁荣之路。
接受他对税法的建议。他建议鼓励工人学习人工智能技能，让企业家更容易获得资本，以及员工所有权和利润分享的新方法。这些并不等同于具有约束力的要求，这些要求将确保工人分享人工智能创造的财富，或者公司支付工人流离失所的成本。
布伦南说： “我对这项政策对未来的影响感到震惊……这已经基于大规模人工智能的采用和人工智能造福社会，我们还没有看到。” “所有这一切都取决于从人工智能的优势中受益。”
Brennan表示，看到诸如修改公司税率或雇佣人员而不是自动化工作的税收优惠等事情，以及防止公司积累巨大市场力量的方法是更有意义的。
Lehane强调扩大人工智能的经济机会，而不是限制潜在的危害，这延伸到了数据中心。他指出了对数据中心的担忧，同时强调了它们可能产生的建筑工作和地方税收收入。然后，他警告说，支持暂停数据中心的政客可能会危及美国在中国的领先地位，甚至将这一立场与2002年授权伊拉克战争的投票相提并论。
Lehane还将儿童安全和教育作为其拟议议程的核心，强调围绕人工智能伴侣为未成年人提供适合年龄的保护和保障的重要性。他还警告不要让人工智能进入教室，认为这样做可能会导致富裕学生与“农村社区儿童”之间的不平等。“但这种观点认为人工智能改善学习是理所当然的，这种说法仍未得到证实，一位批评者表示，与其说人类教师提供更多的资金或个性化关注，不如说值得更多的审查。
Lehane还呼吁制定可执行的人工智能安全标准、独立评估、公众监督，以及限制人工智能系统或使用杀戮开关关闭人工智能系统的能力--尽管最近的研究表明， OpenAI和其他人工智能实验室还没有发布全面的计划，说明如果模型逃脱了人类的控制，他们会怎么做。
布伦南称这些立场“不诚实” ，并指出OpenAI反对旨在实施此类措施的立法的历史。例如， 2024年， OpenAI反对加利福尼亚州的人工智能安全法案SB 1047 ，该法案将强制要求灾难性的风险评估和关闭功能。去年， OpenAI还试图限制国家监管，认为各州可能会破坏美国的创新。该公司最近改变了其中一些职位，支持几项州安全法律，并表示将向公司内部的独立评估人员开放。
Lehane还认为，人们应该保持对使用人工智能做出的重要决策的控制，而不是将判断权完全交给机器。但这提出了一个问题，即在一个人类越来越需要在教育、工作、医疗保健和政府中使用人工智能的社会中，人类的控制到底是什么样子。
在整篇文章中， Lehane将人工智能视为一种技术，可以让美国人恢复他们的代理意识和经济机会。但他将普通美国人的“中产阶级”成功与参与OpenAI等公司日益塑造的经济联系起来。他的政策是否有意义地重新分配权力或巧妙地巩固权力尚不清楚。
TechCrunch联系了OpenAI ，以获得有关Lehane提案和公司立场的更多细节，但截至发布时，它没有回应。

fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Sometimes, GIFs can say what a thousand words can’t. A quick peek at my group chats would prove just that — there’s no shortage of ways to communicate without actually typing a word. I’ve normally relied on repositories like Giphy and Tenor for my GIF needs, though this popular AI tool might soon give me, and you, a way to give GIFs a more personal touch.
The tool I’m talking about is ChatGPT, and in addition to image generation, it will now also let you generate and edit GIFS, as highlighted by The Verge.

The development is part of OpenAI’s new Images 2.6 model, and it should allow users to turn text prompts and uploaded photos into short animated GIFs. For reference, ChatGPT can already generate GIFs, but they’re not truly animated. The current implementation simply simulates movement by placing two slightly different frames side by side. The new GIF generation ability, although not out yet, appears much different.

In a shared example, which highlights the feature in action, it looks like ChatGPT will be able to generate multiple frames of an image and play them in quick succession. Users will also be able to adjust playback speed, with options ranging from 0.5x to 2x. Existing options like the Edit prompt box and the option to resize or remove elements remain.

The options here are endless. You’ll be able to turn a photo of yourself into looping animations, expressing different emotions. You’ll essentially be able to save GIFs of yourself expressing emotions like happiness, sadness, anger, excitement, surprise, and more. Think of it like bitmojis, but animated GIFs with you in them.

In addition to GIF support, expect the update to bring faster image generation to ChatGPT. According to the company, compared to September, users are now already generating roughly 1 billion more images per week. The improvement in generation speed, paired with GIF support, should now help push that number even further.
Images 2.6 is rolling out to all ChatGPT and Codex users across web, desktop, and mobile apps now.

DuckDuckGo is pitching itself to schools after Google created an opening for the alternative search engine. On Tuesday, Google told schools they could turn off Gemini, but it said shutting off its other AI features would cost schools Google Search, as well.

DuckDuckGo, a company that focuses on user privacy by limiting data collection, clearly sees this as a moment to make inroads in education, where Google has historically dominated. According to figures Google has published in previous years, there are around 50 million Chromebooks in schools, used by students and educators, and its Google Classroom platform serves over 150 million users globally.

On X, DuckDuckGo’s founder and CEO, Gabriel Weinberg, pointed to the company’s online documentation, explaining how schools can switch their default search engine to DuckDuckGo’s service instead, adding, “get in touch for help.”

Meanwhile, DuckDuckGo’s chief public affairs officer, Kamyl Bazbaz, issued a stronger statement, writing, “Forcing AI on school children: how a monopolist behaves when they think people are powerless. Prove Google wrong.”
Forcing AI on school children: how a monopolist behaves when they think people are powerless.Prove Google wrong. https://t.co/Ta6ibmFdb9
In an email to TechCrunch, DuckDuckGo chastised Google for its decision, adding that Google could easily turn off Search’s AI features for schools if it wanted to.

The company’s comments come as the American public is weighing how much AI they want to allow into their lives. As Tuesday night’s elections indicate, they don’t want AI data centers built in their towns. But using AI at work and school has become a common practice and requires a more nuanced discussion.

Knowing that educators have struggled with AI, Google developed technology called “Guided Learning” that is meant to help kids learn by walking through problem-solving steps rather than just providing them with an answer. But educators are still asking for tools that let them remove AI from the learning process altogether.

After the backlash on Tuesday, Google defended its decision, saying it was just responding to schools’ feedback. It said that Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search would be off by default, and schools could choose to enable them individually.

We want to clarify what we announced today about our education services. Today’s announcements give schools more choice, not less. Here’s what we announced:– Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search will be OFF 🔴 by default. This is based on K-12 schools asking for more control…
The problem, of course, is that Google Search now heavily uses AI, through AI Overviews and a conversational AI Mode that answers users’ queries.
DuckDuckGo isn’t anti-AI, to be clear — it offers its own set of AI features, including a chat interface called Duck.ai and an AI search assistant.

However, unlike Google, it provides options to disable these features in both its search and browser settings, the company says. It also offers a dedicated website, noai.duckduckgo.com, where AI-assisted answers, AI-generated images, and AI feature suggestions are all turned off.
That flexibility may be driving demand for its services, as the company reported earlier this year that its app installs were up 30% as users rejected being force-fed Google’s AI Search.

fulltext: You can use ChatGPT to edit a GIF’s animation speed and individual frames.

ChatGPT can now create GIFs using a prompt or a photo uploaded to the AI chatbot. The update, which is rolling out alongside OpenAI’s new Images 2.6 model, allows you to adjust the GIF’s animation speed, edit individual frames, and share it with others.

Before this change, ChatGPT couldn’t natively generate GIFs in a single step. An example shared by the company shows how ChatGPT can generate a GIF in response to the prompt, “can you make a gif of a cat dancing?” while also providing you with the option to change the playback speed and view it frame by frame.

Along with support for GIF-making, the Images 2.6 update also enables faster image generation in ChatGPT, OpenAI says. The company says users now generate over 4 billion images per week across ChatGPT and its API, a jump from the 3 billion per week it reported in September.

Images 2.6 is rolling out to all ChatGPT and Codex users across web, desktop, and mobile apps. OpenAI is also launching GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst in its API for faster and higher-quality image generation.

cards.title: Dharma Field Extractor: Any Document In, Structured Fields in JSON Out
cards.title_cn: Dharma Field Extractor ：任何文档输入， JSON中的结构化字段输出
cards.summary: 【Hugging Face 官方动态】Dharma Field Extractor: Any Document In, Structured Fields in JSON Out
fulltext: A 2-billion-parameter model that extracts exactly the fields you ask for, from any document type, outperforming every frontier LLM we tested, at a fraction of the cost.

In April, we released DharmaOCR-LITE, a model specialized for OCR across a wide range of documents, from contracts and court filings to invoices, IDs and forms. The paper behind it made a narrow, well-measured case for domain specialization: a smaller model trained closer to its task beating general-purpose frontier APIs on that task.

OCR gives you the text on a page, faithful to the original formatting. That's exactly what you want when the job is the whole document, like a contract you'll read end to end or a manuscript you're digitizing.

However, there's a different use case: you don't want the page, you want specific fields out of it, in a shape a system downstream can consume. Every line item on an invoice, as a list. The patient name, exam type and date from a medical requisition, ready to schedule. The fields off an ID, mapped to the columns of an employee record.

Run that document through OCR and you get back everything printed on it, line by line, with no indication of which string is the exam type, which is the date or which number is the total. Someone still has to write the code that maps each value to the right field before it reaches the database.

A general-purpose LLM can do this work today, with careful prompting. At frontier API pricing and latency, on a task many businesses need to run at high volume, that quickly becomes the expensive way to solve a well-defined problem.

So we built a model for it instead. The Field Extractor takes a document image and either a request for everything it can find, or an exact schema to fill, and returns structured JSON: typed, field by field, nested where the document nests. An invoice comes back with every line item as an ordered list, each with its own quantity and value, alongside the totals. An ID comes back as the fields you'll store, under the names your system already uses for them. The same checkpoint handles all of it, with no per-type fine-tuning.
You can try it yourself here.

Say a batch of supplier invoices lands every morning, and you need four things off each one to push into your system: the supplier, the invoice number, the due date, the total. Same story for medical requisitions going into a scheduler, or contracts feeding a compliance system, where what matters is the parties, the term, the penalties and the fine amounts. You don't need the page, you need certain fields. With the Field Extractor there are two ways to ask for them:

The choice comes down to what you already know. Send an open request when you don't know what the document holds. Send a schema when the output has to match a shape that already exists somewhere else.

Either way, what comes back is JSON: the fields as keys, the values typed as requested, and null where the document didn't have what you asked for. When you send a schema, the output follows it exactly, with the same keys and no extra fields, so it can go straight into the next system.

The base model is DharmaOCR-LITE v1.1, a new 2-billion-parameter version optimized from the one in the paper and already specialized for OCR through supervised fine-tuning and DPO. On top of that checkpoint we trained a LoRA adapter on 43,384 training examples covering both request modes.
The data is organized into three streams:

All three streams are annotated at the field level. The mix is deliberately multi-domain: receipts, commercial invoices, forms, bank statements, ID documents and synthetic documents, rather than one filing type.

The full benchmark covers 546 documents across three request scenarios, for 1,638 total cases: extracting every field with no schema, a partial schema naming only real fields, and a schema that also includes deliberately nonexistent fields. The score is field-level F1 (matched by path, including position inside a table), multiplied by the Levenshtein similarity on the values that matched and by the share of outputs that come back as valid JSON.
We ran the same benchmark against four general-purpose frontier configurations.
Against general-purpose LLMs, the quality gap runs from 1.8 points (Claude Opus 5, the closest) to 9.3 points (GPT-5.6 Luna, the widest).

Cost runs from roughly 6 times lower (GPT-5.6 Luna) to roughly 147 times lower (GPT-5.6 Sol). The two sides are priced differently. The frontier figures come from measured average input and output tokens per page, reasoning tokens included, against each provider's published list pricing. Every frontier model ran with reasoning set to low; Claude Opus 5 used adaptive effort, which can skip reasoning on simpler pages while staying at the low level. Ours isn't billed per token: the model runs self-hosted, so the figure is GPU time on a single L40S at $2.24 per hour.

This is not a sales price. Self-hosted cost depends on the hardware, the volume and the latency each deployment needs. The comparison is here to show that a sovereign SSLM, deployed on your own infrastructure, is a real alternative to frontier APIs.
SROIE and FUNSD are two public datasets in our benchmark, not used in training. Below is one example from each.

On a SROIE receipt, we asked for all 18 fields printed on it, with no phantom fields this time, and every one comes back correct: the multi-line, unlabeled billing address captured as a single field, the two blank fields (salesperson and ref) correctly returned as null, and every number on the receipt matching to the cent.

On a FUNSD photocopying variance form, a checklist of twelve boolean fields with one nested group of five sub-options, the model marks exactly the one box that's checked (poor quality original, with a handwritten "faded" note beside it) as true, and the other eleven as false, matching the form exactly. It also reads the handwritten Bates ID off the page correctly, and returns null for the two fields left blank.

A 2-billion-parameter model scored 0.834, above every frontier configuration we tested, from Claude Opus 5 at 0.816 to GPT-5.6 Luna at 0.741, while running on a single L40S at a lower cost per extraction than every API in the comparison. Higher quality and lower cost, measured on the same benchmark, in the same run.

This isn't the first time we've measured it. Our OCR paper put the first DharmaOCR-LITE, a 3-billion-parameter model, above every commercial frontier API tested on Brazilian Portuguese; three months later, newer and better-resourced models arrived, and the gap held. Now a 2-billion-parameter model does it on field extraction. Each result adds evidence for the thesis we started Dharma-AI with: on a bounded task, a small model trained close to that task beats a frontier model asked to do the same thing in general. In this benchmark, it also cost 6 to 147 times less to run.
Parameter count sets the ceiling; training decides how much of it a model reaches on your task. Your business doesn't need the biggest model available. It needs one trained for your problem.

fulltext_cn: 这是一个20亿参数的模型，可从任何文档类型中准确提取您要求的字段，其性能优于我们测试的每个前沿法学硕士，成本仅为前沿法学硕士的一小部分。
4月，我们发布了DharmaOCR-LITE ，这是一种专门针对OCR的模型，适用于各种文件，从合同和法院文件到发票、身份证件和表格。其背后的论文为领域专业化提出了一个狭隘的、经过精心测量的案例：一个更接近其任务的较小模型，在该任务上击败了通用前沿API。
OCR为您提供页面上的文本，忠实于原始格式。当工作是整个文件时，这正是你想要的，比如你将端到端阅读的合同或你正在数字化的手稿。
但是，有一个不同的用例：您不想要页面，您希望从中删除特定字段，形成下游系统可以使用的形状。发票上的每个行项目，作为列表。医疗请购单中的患者姓名、检查类型和日期，可随时安排。ID上的字段，映射到员工记录的列。
通过OCR运行该文档，您可以逐行取回打印在其上的所有内容，而不指示哪个字符串是考试类型，哪个是日期或哪个数字是总数。在每个值到达数据库之前，仍然需要有人编写代码，将每个值映射到正确的字段。
通用法学硕士今天可以在仔细的提示下完成这项工作。在前沿API定价和延迟方面，对于许多企业需要以高容量运行的任务，这很快成为解决明确定义问题的昂贵方法。
因此，我们为它构建了一个模型。字段提取器获取文档图像以及它可以找到的所有内容的请求或要填写的确切架构，并返回结构化JSON ：类型化，逐字段，嵌套在文档嵌套的位置。发票以有序列表的形式返回每个行项目，每个行项目都有自己的数量和价值，以及总计。身份证件将作为您将存储的字段返回，并显示在您的系统已为其使用的名称下。相同的检查点处理所有问题，无需每种类型的微调。
您可以在这里亲自尝试。
假设每天早上都有一批供应商发票，每张发票都需要四样东西才能推送到您的系统中：供应商、发票编号、截止日期、总金额。对于进入调度程序的医疗请购单或提供合规系统的合同，同样的情况，重要的是各方、期限、罚款和罚款金额。您不需要页面，您需要某些字段。使用Field Extractor ，有两种方法可以请求它们：
选择取决于您已经知道的内容。当您不知道文件包含哪些内容时，请发送未结申请。当输出必须与其他地方已存在的形状匹配时，发送架构。
无论哪种方式，返回的是JSON ：字段作为键，键入为请求的值，以及在文档没有您所要求的内容时为null。当您发送架构时，输出完全遵循它，具有相同的键，没有额外的字段，因此它可以直接进入下一个系统。
基础模型是DharmaOCR-LITE v1.1 ，这是从论文中优化的一个新的20亿参数版本，已经通过监督微调和DPO专门用于OCR。在该检查点之上，我们在涵盖两种请求模式的43,384个训练示例上训练了一个LoRA适配器。
数据分为三个流：
所有三个流都会在字段级别进行注释。混合是故意多领域的：收据、商业发票、表格、银行对账单、身份证明文件和综合文件，而不是一种归档类型。
完整的基准测试涵盖了三个请求场景中的546个文档，总共1,638个案例：提取没有模式的每个字段，仅命名真实字段的部分模式，以及还包括故意不存在字段的模式。分数是字段级F1 （通过路径匹配，包括表内的位置） ，乘以匹配值的Levenshtein相似性以及作为有效JSON返回的输出份额。
我们对四种通用前沿配置进行了相同的基准测试。
与通用LLM相比，质量差距从1.8分（ Claude Opus 5 ，最接近）到9.3分（ GPT-5.6 Luna ，最宽）。

成本从大约6倍低（ GPT-5.6 LUNA ）到大约147倍低（ GPT-5.6 SOL ）。双方的定价不同。前沿数据来自每页测量的平均输入和输出令牌，包括推理令牌，以及每个提供商发布的列表定价。每个前沿模型都将推理设置为低级； Claude Opus 5使用了自适应努力，它可以跳过简单页面上的推理，同时保持在低级。我们不按令牌收费：该模型自托管运行，因此该数字是单个L40S上的GPU时间，每小时$ 2.24。
这不是销售价格。自托管成本取决于每个部署所需的硬件、卷和延迟。这里的比较表明，部署在您自己的基础设施上的主权SSLM是前沿API的真正替代品。
SROIE和FUNSD是我们基准中的两个公共数据集，未用于培训。以下是每个例子中的一个。
在SROIE收据上，我们要求打印所有18个字段，这次没有虚拟字段，每个字段都正确返回：多行、未标记的账单地址作为单个字段捕获，两个空白字段（销售人员和参考）正确返回为空，收据上的每个数字都与分数匹配。
在FUNSD复印方差表上，由12个布尔字段组成的清单，其中一个嵌套组包含5个子选项，模型将选中的一个框（原始质量差，旁边有一个手写的“褪色”注释）标记为真，其他11个标记为假，与表单完全匹配。它还正确地从页面上读取手写的Bates ID ，并对留空的两个字段返回null。
一个20亿参数的模型得分为0.834 ，高于我们测试的每个前沿配置，从0.816的Claude Opus 5到0.741的GPT-5.6 Luna ，同时在单个L40S上运行，每次提取的成本低于比较中的每个API。在同一运行中，在同一基准上测量更高的质量和更低的成本。

这不是我们第一次测量它。我们的OCR论文将第一个DharmaOCR-LITE （一个30亿参数的模型）置于在巴西葡萄牙语上测试的每个商业前沿API之上；三个月后，更新、资源更好的模型到达，差距依然存在。现在，一个20亿参数的模型可以在现场提取上做到这一点。每个结果都为我们开始Dharma-AI的论文提供了证据：在有界任务上，接近该任务训练的小模型通常会击败被要求做同样事情的前沿模型。在这个基准中，它的运行成本也降低了6到147倍。
